_: Pack policy: the vanilla recipes Project Nauvis takes away. tools/gen_removals.py turns this into condition-false recipe files in the nauvis pack mod. See docs/MAPPING.md.
_rule: A vanilla recipe is removed only when the pack can already do that job. `replaced_by` names the pack recipe that does it, and the build fails if that recipe is not shipped - so nothing can be taken away and left with nothing in its place. That is also why this list is short: most of Factorio is not built yet.
_why: Two kinds of entry. A *conflict* is a vanilla recipe making an item the mapping maps a Factorio item onto, so two recipes with different ingredient lists produce the same thing and one of them is wrong - non-negotiable #1. A *bypass* is vanilla doing a job Factorio has a machine for, where keeping it would make that machine pointless.
_mirrors: Vanilla recipes a pack recipe deliberately reproduces rather than replaces - same ingredients, same count, reachable both ways. The conflict check stands down for these, because the two are not in disagreement about anything; without the entry it would demand vanilla's removal and take the 2x2 inventory route away for no reason.

mirrors.minecraft:oak_planks: nauvis:oak_planks makes four planks from one oak log, which is what vanilla's does. It exists so the whole opening - logs, planks, pickaxe - is in the crafting panel, not so the bench version has to go.

_kept: Vanilla recipes that make a mapped item out of that same item in another shape - a block back into nine ingots, nine nuggets into one. They are not a second way of making iron plates, they are iron changing shape, and Factorio has no nuggets or storage blocks to have an opinion about. The conflict check stands down for these too; each says why.

kept.minecraft:iron_ingot_from_iron_block: Nine ingots went in, nine come out. Storage, not smelting.
kept.minecraft:iron_ingot_from_nuggets: Nuggets only ever come from ingots or from smelting tools, so this is iron changing shape.
kept.minecraft:copper_ingot: The copper block back into nine ingots. Storage, not smelting.
kept.minecraft:copper_ingot_from_waxed_copper: The same block with wax on it.
kept.minecraft:copper_ingot_from_nuggets: Copper nuggets, the same argument as iron's.

minecraft:chest.note: Factorio's wooden chest is four wood; vanilla's is eight planks. The mapping makes minecraft:chest the wooden chest, so vanilla's price is simply the wrong one.

minecraft:furnace.note: The stone furnace is a machine of the pack's own now, five stone and two tiles by two, and it smelts Factorio's recipes at Factorio's times. A vanilla furnace beside it would smelt the same ore at vanilla's price and its own pace, and would be the one every Minecraft player reached for first.

minecraft:iron_ingot_from_smelting_raw_i.note: Iron plate is one iron ore in 3.5 seconds, in a furnace of the pack's. Vanilla's is the same ore in ten.

minecraft:iron_ingot_from_blasting_raw_i.note: The blast furnace's copy of the same recipe.

minecraft:iron_ingot_from_smelting_iron_.note: The silk-touched ore block. Factorio's iron ore is the raw item, and the pack maps it there; a block that smelts into a plate would be a second ore.

minecraft:iron_ingot_from_smelting_deeps.note: The deepslate ore block, the same argument.

minecraft:copper_ingot_from_smelting_raw.note: Copper plate, the same as iron's.

minecraft:stone_bricks.note: Factorio smelts two stone into one brick; vanilla crafts four stone into four. Ratios differ, and non-negotiable #1 says which is right.

minecraft:stone_bricks_from_stone_stonec.note: The stonecutter's copy of the same recipe.

minecraft:hopper.note: The hopper is an inserter that needs no power, no facing decision and no thought, and it is the one vanilla block that makes Factorio's signature machine pointless. The burner inserter replaces it and is cheaper - one iron gear wheel and one iron plate - so what is lost is the free ride, not the ability.

minecraft:stone_pickaxe.note: Four planks, not three stone and two sticks. A stone pickaxe made of stone cannot be the first pickaxe, because the first pickaxe is how you get stone - and this pack needs the tool ladder to be one step rather than five.

minecraft:wooden_pickaxe.note: The rung the stone pickaxe now stands on. Keeping it would mean crafting a worse pickaxe to reach a better one that costs the same wood.

minecraft:hopper_minecart.note: A hopper on rails is still a hopper. The plain minecart and the chest minecart stay: nothing of the pack's does their job, and a vanilla recipe goes only when the pack can already do that job.

minecraft:cobblestone_wall.note: Factorio's stone wall is five stone bricks; vanilla's cobblestone wall is six cobblestone. The wall is the same block, behind stone-wall research.

minecraft:cobblestone_wall_from_cobblest.note: The stonecutter's route to the same wall, at vanilla's price of one cobblestone or stone a wall. Factorio's wall is five stone bricks and behind research.

minecraft:cobblestone_wall_from_stone_st.note: The stonecutter's route to the same wall, at vanilla's price of one cobblestone or stone a wall. Factorio's wall is five stone bricks and behind research.
